To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
intranasal oxytocin enhances attention towards the eyes in non-human primates, and that this effect of oxytocin on attention is specific for the eyes.

1) intranasal oxytocin increases attention to the eye-region of faces in rhesus monkey, 2) oxytocin has this effect even when the eyes are not the first thing the monkey sees, 3) this effect of oxytocin is not due to an overall increase in attention, and 4) this effect is not due to a preference for the eye-region of the face.
oxytocin enhances attentional bias to the eye region of the face in rhesus monkey.
